purpose: Provide an original-inspired playful eye option with a broad curved almond silhouette.

arguments.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: transparent cartoon game sprite variation for SLEVEJM3.BMP-004
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target and absolute authority for the shark body, waves, yellow mermaid hair, palette, linework, placement, framing, and transparent canvas. Images 2 and 3 are the exact original low-resolution frame and enlarged nearest-neighbor reference; use them only as authority for the eye's playful asymmetry.
Primary request: Change only the shark's single visible lower/right eye in Image 1. Give it a broad, curved almond shape derived from the original pixel eye: both the upper and lower white contours bow outward, the upper contour is gently lifted rather than angled down, the outer/front end is round, and the inner/rear end tapers softly without becoming a sharp triangle. Keep the eye generously open. Add one round black pupil looking forward/right toward the yellow hair, positioned away from the tapered inner corner, with one small friendly catchlight. The result must read playful, eager, and delighted, like an excited cartoon character.
Constraints: Retain exactly one visible eye in the same lower/right facial location. Keep the upper gray forehead completely clean, with no second eye, no stray dark mark, and no separate eyebrow or brow ridge. Preserve every other pixel-level design decision from Image 1 as closely as possible: identical shark silhouette, dorsal fin, highlights, gray shading, snout, body pose, water waves, cyan outlines, yellow hair, black outlines, cropping, scale, and genuinely transparent background. No mouth or teeth changes. No new objects, text, or watermark.
Avoid: perfect circle; tall upright oval; straight or downward-sloping upper eyelid; triangular eye; narrow slit; sharp predatory eye; hostile, dangerous, angry, devious, sleepy, suspicious, or frowning expression; brow; eyelashes; second facial mark; body restyling.
